claim: LLM benchmark performance across a 60-model x 44-benchmark matrix is intrinsically low-rank: a small number of latent factors capture most of the structure in the full task space.
stance_target: correlated/latent-factor structure underlies apparently diverse LLM capability measurements
scope_conditions: 60 LLMs x 44 general-purpose benchmarks (not code-specific, not requirement-level)
quoted_support: we apply Factor Analysis (FA) to a massive performance matrix of LLMs versus benchmarks (60x44) revealing an intrinsically low-rank structure of that matrix.

claim: Latent factors extracted via Factor Analysis correspond to coherent, skill-like dimensions of LLM behavior rather than benchmark-specific noise.
stance_target: existence of interpretable latent skills underlying code/LLM competence
scope_conditions: general LLM benchmarks, not code generation specifically
quoted_support: We further show that these latent factors correspond to coherent, skill-like, dimensions of LLM behavior.

claim: A low-rank latent skill space enables profiling new models from a small subset of tasks and identifying redundant benchmark tasks.
stance_target: practical value of latent-factor decomposition for evaluation efficiency
quoted_support: Leveraging this latent skill-space, we deliver three practical tools for LLM evaluation and downstream users: (i) identifying redundant tasks, (ii) profiling new models using a small subset of tasks, and (iii) selecting models aligned with desired skill profiles.
